evidence:
Source review only. No configured judge run exists for this candidate (raw-evidence-index.json scope: 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and target/Oracle scores are absent'), so how the judge actually applies the plural and unchanged wording is NOT EXERCISED. The scripted golden runs do not measure it.

WHAT HOLDS (every plural/unchanged instance I found, by criterion id in tests/scored/functional/judge.toml unless stated):
- hro_referrer_roster: 'every supplied referring employee (Dara Whitfield, Sofia Marchetti and Omar Haddad)' - the collection is enumerated and functional/prompt.md P1 says 'Exercise availability of all three supplied referrers'.
- hro_anon_read_status: 'inventory all distinct operational read families ... Each must return401', with dedup of a shared bootstrap and 'report bounded coverage'; P9 repeats 'For every family capture populated authenticated success'.
- hro_change_readers: 'every supplied signed-in role can navigate to saved coordinated previews and receipts'; B5 already signs in as each other demo account, and the seven accounts are listed in app_context.md.
- hro_change_audit ('every successful member revision produces a readable audit line'), hro_change_lineage ('each selected source ... exactly one current COMMITTED successor'), hro_change_afterimages ('All member headrooms reflect the same complete transaction'), hro_change_receipt ('all old/new offers ... complete before/after headrooms'), hro_change_net_budget ('Each touched budget'): B1 fixes the collection at two members and two requisitions, all inspected.
- hro_desk_figures: 'marks only its destination requisition over budget' and 'every figure that both the editor and the saved preview display is the same in both' - D1 reads both members and both touched requisitions.
- hro_desk_remove_member: 'The remaining three keep their selected offers, destinations and every typed term exactly'; D3 records all three remaining members. Members are identified 'by their selected offer and typed values, not by a position label', so a legitimate renumbering is not punished.
- hro_desk_field_refusal: 'the other members' inputs are not marked' and 'All other entries stay as typed' on a two-member entry (D4), with the corrected save as positive control.
- hro_live_source_flag: flagged member AND the unflagged first member are both read. The guard is 'if the other member's entries change' - entries, not computed figures - so a legitimate live refresh of headroom or of the preview's out-of-date mark is not charged.
- Exactly-one rows: hro_competing, hro_concurrent_approval/revision/rescission, hro_change_overlap, hro_change_retry_concurrent, hro_restart ('seed IDs remain exactly once'), and tests/gates/constraints hro_gate_shared ('Exactly one of each saved identity must be present'). Each names the records to re-read for both winner and loser; none prescribes a winner or timing.
- hro_stale_revision and hro_stale_rescission each list three refusal targets and say 'all refuse'; hro_date_rejection lists four invalid cases; hro_change_shape lists every invalid shape. hro_referral_immutable says 'need all three operation kinds'.
- hro_draft_eligibility adapts one DRAFT identity, but hireops_rules.md:215 says 'One row in the export sits at DRAFT', so one is the whole collection.

UNCHANGED GUARDS VS LEGITIMATE SIDE EFFECTS:
- functional/prompt.md (paragraph beginning 'Record before/after facts per row and per record'): 'A rejection may add generic access/security logging; it must not create a successful settlement entry or change economic state. Actions may add ordinary extra audit entries, so do not demand exact global counts.' This global allowance covers the rows that do not restate it (hro_change_stale_leaf, hro_change_aba, hro_change_anon_prepare/commit, hro_anon_*). It matches hireops_rules.md:472-474 ('generic access logs may grow. A draft record can remain after a conflict').
- Restated locally in hro_stale_approval/revision/rescission ('Generic access/security logs may grow'), hro_change_over_budget ('a draft and generic access logs may remain'), hro_change_preview_neutral ('Generic access logging and the draft itself may grow'), hro_change_prepare_* ('generic security/access logs are allowed').
- hro_whatif_roles: 'an ordinary sign-in audit line and the person's own unsent entries are not such records' and 'a successful response from a calculation that saves nothing is not a failure' - mirrors hireops_rules.md:538-540.
- hro_change_stale_leaf baselines on 'immediately before the attempt', i.e. after the other user's legitimate revision, so that revision is not counted as a change.
- hro_history / hro_revision_ledger_history: 'the same rows retain their original amounts, identities and links; corrections are new entries' - consistent with the append-only rule at hireops_rules.md:374-378; the superseded marker lives on the offer row, not the ledger row.
- hro_anon_req_create and hro_anon_offer_create replay with 'a fresh unique title' / 'a fresh candidate', so absence is checked by identity rather than by count. test.sh:207 runs rewardkit with '--max-concurrent-agent 1', and functional/prompt.md tells the judge the gates' requisition and PENDING offer are 'existing shared state', so another judge's records cannot trip an unchanged guard.
- hro_restart requires records to 'survive identically' but P10 says 'reopen/sign in', so the lost session is not charged.

UNRESOLVED INSTANCES (both P3, wording/coverage, no observed impact):
1. hro_whatif_roles (weight 4) samples two of the six non-Finance roles. Public rule, hireops_rules.md:537: 'Every signed-in role can use the editor to work out a hypothetical change'; app_context.md: 'all signed-in roles ... can work a hypothetical change out in the same editor'. The criterion says 'sign in as Auditor ... Repeat as Recruiter' and 'Owns the positive what-if for non-Finance roles'; D2 exercises the same two. Comp partner and the three Approvers are never asked to open the editor. No other criterion covers it: hro_change_readers owns reading saved previews/receipts, and the hro_change_prepare_*/commit_* rows own the 403.
2. hro_referral_creation: 'P4 approval: exactly one10000.00 accrual to employee Dara Whitfield, not candidate'. Dara is also the prescribed referrer in P6 ('referrer Dara'), in B1 for both hires, and in hro_competing, so by the end of the run the Referrals view legitimately holds several 10000.00 Dara accruals. The scope to the P4 offer is carried only by the 'P4 approval:' prefix and by P4's 'Record ... immediately'. A judge reading the Referrals list late and counting per employee could fail a correct app. hro_change_referral and hro_referral_immutable are scoped correctly ('attached to its original offer', 'that original accrual').
counterexample: Instance 1 (broken app that passes): an editor rendered for Finance, Auditor and Recruiter only, hidden for Comp partner and the three Approvers, earns full hro_whatif_roles credit while breaking hireops_rules.md:537. I judge this unlikely in practice (role gating is normally Finance-only or all-roles, and the Recruiter sample catches a gate keyed on the Auditor named in the brief), which is why this is a Note and not a Fail. Instance 2 (conforming app that could fail): a correct app is read on the Referrals screen after P6/B1 have run; a judge counting Dara Whitfield's 10000.00 accruals finds four or more and scores hro_referral_creation 0 on 'exactly one'. Neither was observed in a run.
suggested_fix: 1. In hro_whatif_roles and D2, add one more sampled role from the Comp partner/Approver group, or state in the criterion that Auditor and Recruiter are the sampled witnesses for the every-role rule; do not add four more full what-if passes without a measured workload reason. 2. In hro_referral_creation, change 'exactly one10000.00 accrual to employee Dara Whitfield' to 'exactly one10000.00 accrual for this P4 offer, credited to employee Dara Whitfield'. Both are task-specific criterion wording; no harness or reward-policy change is involved. A configured judge run is still needed to exercise this row.
